extracted.intended_audience: parties, counsel, petitioners, and participants in NRC adjudications and rulemaking proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for discovery, evidence, motions, initial decisions, and petitions for rulemaking before the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 CFR part 2, subparts governing adjudications and rulemaking. Covers content, timing, disclosures, protections for Safeguards Information, and NRC actions on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of discovery requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may request another party to produce and permit inspection and copying of any designated documents, or inspect, copy, test, or sample tangible things which are within the scope of § 2.704 and which are in the possession, custody, or control of the party upon whom the request is served; or permit entry upon designated land or other property in the possession or control of the party for inspection, measuring, surveying, photographing, testing, or sampling within the scope of § 2.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be limited to items within § 2.704; may include access onto property for inspection or measurement; production of NRC records or documents is treated separately under §§ 2.709 and 2.390.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service timing for discovery requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The request may be served on any party without leave of the Commission or the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as otherwise provided in § 2.704, the request may be served after the proceeding is set for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a discovery request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify the items to be inspected either by individual item or by category, and describe each item and category with reasonable particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must specify a reasonable time, place, and manner of making the inspection and performing the related acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and content for discovery requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The party upon whom the request is served shall serve a written response within thirty (30) days after service of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must state for each item or category whether inspection and related activities will be permitted as requested, or set forth the reasons for objection; if objection is to part of an item or category, the part must be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for NRC records in general discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (a) through (d) related to production and inspection do not apply to production for inspection and copying or photographing of NRC records or documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production of NRC records is subject instead to the provisions of §§ 2.709 and 2.390.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for admissions — scope and content
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after its answer has been filed, a party may file a written request for the admission of the genuineness and authenticity of any relevant document described in or attached to the request, or for the admission of the truth of any specified relevant matter of fact. A copy of the document must be delivered with the request unless already furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions may be used in evidence to the same extent and subject to the same objections as other admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to requests for admissions and deemed admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each requested admission is considered made unless, within a time designated by the presiding officer and not less than ten (10) days after service, the party serves either a sworn statement denying specifically the matters or setting forth in detail reasons why it can neither truthfully admit nor deny; or written objections on grounds of privilege, irrelevance, or impropriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers on matters objected to may be deferred until objections are determined. If written objections are made to only part of a request, the remainder must be answered in time designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of NRC staff witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings where NRC staff is a party, the NRC staff will make available one or more witnesses, designated by the Executive Director for Operations or a delegee, for oral examination at the hearing or on deposition regarding any matter, not privileged, that is relevant to the issues in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attendance and testimony of the Commissioners and named NRC personnel may not be required normally; the presiding officer may require attendance of named personnel upon a showing of exceptional circumstances (e.g., unique direct personal knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories to NRC personnel — presiding officer's authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file with the presiding officer written interrogatories to be answered by NRC personnel designated by the Executive Director for Operations or a delegee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may require answers if it finds the answers are necessary to a proper decision and not reasonably obtainable from any other source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limit on depositions/answers of named NRC employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposition of a particular named NRC employee or answer to interrogatories by NRC personnel may not be required before the matters in controversy have been identified by order of the Commission or presiding officer, or after the beginning of the prehearing conference, except upon leave of the presiding officer for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects named personnel from premature or delayed discovery absent good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of §§ 2.704(c) and (e) to interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of § 2.704(c) and (e) apply to interrogatories served under this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope and limits in § 2.704 govern interrogatory practice when applied to NRC personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of records in custody of Commissioners and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Records or documents in the custody of the Commissioners and NRC personnel are available for inspection and copying or photographing under paragraph (b) of § 2.709 and § 2.390.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such availability is subject to the exemptions and procedures in § 2.390.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory initial disclosures by NRC staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent stipulated or directed otherwise, the NRC staff shall provide to other parties within 45 days after issuance of a prehearing conference order following the initial prehearing conference, and without awaiting a discovery request: (A) all NRC staff documents, data compilations, or other tangible things in possession, custody, or control that are relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity in the pleadings (except privileged/protected items), including Office of Investigations and Office of Enforcement reports and exhibits; and (B) a list of documents for which a claim of privilege or protected status is being made with sufficient information to assess the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When required documents are publicly available (e.g., NRC Web site, Public Document Room), a sufficient disclosure may be the location, title, and page reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to update disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of disclosure under § 2.709 is continuing. A disclosure update must be made every month after initial disclosures on a due date selected by the presiding officer, unless parties agree otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates are limited to documents subject to disclosure and need not include documents developed, obtained, or discovered during the two weeks before the due date; include any documents not previously disclosed; duty to update ends when presiding officer issues a decision resolving that dispute issue, or as otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for publicly available documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When any document, data compilation, or other tangible thing that must be disclosed is publicly available, a sufficient disclosure shall identify the location (including ADAMS accession number when available), the title, and a page reference to the relevant item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This satisfies disclosure obligations without producing copies when public sources suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request requirements for NRC records in initial licensing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for production of an NRC record or document not available under § 2.390 by a party to an initial licensing proceeding may be served on the Executive Director for Operations or a delegee without leave of the Commission or presiding officer. The request must identify the records or documents, by item or category, describe each with reasonable particularity, and state why the record is relevant to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the procedural route to obtain NRC-held records not otherwise publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Director's objection to production
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Executive Director for Operations or a delegee objects to producing a requested record or document on grounds of irrelevance or exemption under § 2.390, or that disclosure is not necessary or reasonably obtainable elsewhere, the Executive Director shall advise the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objection must be communicated so the requesting party may seek relief from the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to compel production of NRC records
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Executive Director objects, the requesting party may apply to the presiding officer in writing to compel production; the application must set forth the relevancy of the record or document and will be processed as a motion under § 2.323(a)-(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document covered by the application must be produced for in camera inspection of the presiding officer, if requested, and only to the extent necessary to determine relevancy, exemption status under § 2.390, necessity to a proper decision, and whether the information is reasonably obtainable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer's order to produce after findings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the presiding officer determines the requesting party has demonstrated relevancy and that production is not exempt or that if exempt disclosure is necessary to a proper decision and not reasonably obtainable elsewhere, the presiding officer shall order the Executive Director to produce the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer's determination triggers mandatory production subject to any protective terms the officer may impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards Information access prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: For requested documents including Safeguards Information exempt from disclosure under § 2.390, the presiding officer may issue an order requiring disclosure only if: (i) individual seeking access has requisite 'need to know' as defined in 10 CFR 73.2; (ii) individual has undergone an FBI criminal history records check via fingerprints and procedures in 10 CFR 73.57(d) (unless exempt); and (iii) the NRC Office of Administration has found the individual trustworthy and reliable (unless exempt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural protections apply before final adverse determinations; the Office of Administration must provide additional records considered, resolve challenges to completeness/accuracy within 10 days, and adverse determinations may be reviewed by a designated officer upon request within specific timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective terms and conditions for Safeguards Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may include in an order any protective terms and conditions (including affidavits of nondisclosure) as necessary and appropriate to prevent unauthorized disclosure of Safeguards Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective measures may be tailored by the presiding officer to secure information while allowing participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection requirements when Safeguards Information is held by non-staff
rubrics_metrics.description: When Safeguards Information protected from disclosure under Section 147 is received and possessed by anyone other than the NRC staff, it must also be protected according to the requirements of § 73.21 and the requirements of § 73.22 or § 73.23, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External holders of Safeguards Information must comply with NRC security regulations for handling such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing safeguards with procedural rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may prescribe additional procedures to effectively safeguard and prevent disclosure of Safeguards Information to unauthorized persons with minimum impairment of the procedural rights which would be available if Safeguards Information were not involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer should aim to protect sensitive info while preserving litigants' rights to participate meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for unauthorized disclosure of Safeguards Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of a provision for protection of Safeguards Information contained in an order may be subject to a civil penalty imposed under § 2.205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to other sanctions, civil penalties can be imposed for breach of protective orders; criminal penalties may also apply under the Atomic Energy Act as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restriction for discovery requests against NRC staff
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under this section may not be made or entertained before the matters in controversy have been identified by the Commission or the presiding officer, or after the beginning of the prehearing conference under § 2.329, except upon leave of the presiding officer for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing restriction prevents premature or untimely requests for NRC staff records or testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary disposition — filing deadline and required statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may move for summary disposition for all or part of the matters, with or without affidavits; summary disposition motions must be filed no later than 20 days after the close of discovery. The moving party shall attach a short and concise statement of the material facts as to which the moving party contends there is no genuine issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other party may answer within 20 days, attaching a concise statement of facts showing a genuine issue; material facts set forth by the moving party will be considered admitted unless controverted by the opposing party's statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit requirements and opposing burden on summary disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits must set forth facts that would be admissible in evidence and demonstrate affirmatively that the affiant is competent to testify to the matters stated. A party opposing a supported motion may not rest upon mere allegations or denials; the opposition must set forth specific facts showing a genuine issue of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer may permit supplementation by depositions, interrogatory answers, or further affidavits. If no answer is filed, an appropriate decision must be rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief when essential facts cannot be presented in affidavit form
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears from opposing affidavits that the party cannot, for reasons stated, present by affidavit facts essential to justify opposition, the presiding officer may refuse the application, order a continuance to permit affidavits to be obtained, or make another appropriate order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer's determination must be made a matter of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer discretion on timeliness and expedition for summary motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer need not consider a motion for summary disposition unless its resolution will serve to expedite the proceeding if granted. The presiding officer may dismiss summarily or hold in abeyance untimely motions filed shortly before the hearing or during the hearing if responding would require diversion of substantial resources and extend the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions filed late or that would distract from hearing preparation may be denied or deferred to preserve efficient proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting summary disposition and limitation for construction-permit proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall render the decision sought if the filings, depositions, answers to interrogatories, admissions, statements of the parties, and affidavits show no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is entitled to a decision as a matter of law. However, in proceedings involving a construction permit for a production or utilization facility, the procedure may be used only for determination of specific subordinate issues and may not be used to determine the ultimate issue whether the permit shall be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply usual summary judgment-style standard, but do not decide the ultimate permit question in construction-permit proceedings via summary disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for presiding officer decision on summary disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall issue an order no later than forty (40) days after any responses to the summary disposition motion are filed, indicating whether the motion is granted or denied and the bases therefore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a fixed deadline for issuing rulings on summary disposition motions after responses are in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to present evidence and requirement for cross-examination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Every party has the right to present oral or documentary evidence and rebuttal evidence and to conduct, in accordance with an approved cross-examination plan that contains the information specified in paragraph (c), any cross-examination required for full and true disclosure of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination must follow an approved plan (see detailed content requirements) and is integral to a party's rights to test evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written direct testimony — service and admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall submit direct testimony of witnesses in written form unless otherwise ordered. When advance written testimony is used, each party shall serve copies of proposed written testimony on every other party at least fifteen (15) days in advance of the hearing session at which the testimony is to be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer may permit introduction of written testimony not timely served with consent or after reasonable opportunity to examine; written testimony must be offered and admitted as an exhibit or may be incorporated into the transcript at the presiding officer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination plan content and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to conduct cross-examination must be accompanied by a cross-examination plan containing: (i) a brief description of the issues on which cross-examination will be conducted; (ii) the objective to be achieved by cross-examination; and (iii) the proposed line of questions that may logically lead to achieving the objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan may be submitted only to the presiding officer and must be kept confidential until issuance of the initial decision on the issue; the presiding officer shall then provide each plan to the Commission's Secretary for inclusion in the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to written testimony and cross-examination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs on written testimony and cross-examination do not apply to proceedings initiated under subpart B for modification, suspension, or revocation of a license or to proceedings for imposition of a civil penalty, unless otherwise directed by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer has discretion to apply or relax these requirements in certain enforcement or licensing modification proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for proposed findings and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The party who has the burden of proof shall, within thirty (30) days after the record is closed, file proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law and briefs and a proposed form of order or decision. Other parties may file within forty (40) days after the record is closed. A party who has the burden of proof may reply within five (5) days after filing of proposed findings and conclusions by other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deadlines may be modified by order of the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file proposed findings when directed
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file proposed findings of fact, conclusions of law, or briefs when directed to do so may be considered a default, and an order or initial decision may be entered accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with an order to file may result in adverse procedural consequences including default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for proposed findings and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed findings of fact must be clearly and concisely set forth in numbered paragraphs and confined to material issues of fact presented on-the-record, with exact citations to the transcript and exhibits in support of each proposed finding. Proposed conclusions of law must be set forth in numbered paragraphs as to all material issues of law or discretion presented on-the-record. An intervenor's proposed findings and conclusions must be confined to issues which that party placed in controversy or sought to place in controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict form and citation requirements facilitate the presiding officer's decision-making and ensure focus on record-supported issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision — finality, support, and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: After hearing, the presiding officer will render an initial decision which will constitute the final action of the Commission forty (40) days after its date unless a party petitions for Commission review or the Commission takes review sua sponte. An initial decision will be in writing and based on the whole record and supported by reliable, probative, and substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial decision must include: (1) findings, conclusions, and rulings with reasons on all material issues presented on-the-record; (2) all facts officially noticed and relied on; (3) the appropriate ruling, order, or denial of relief with effective date; and (4) the times for filing petitions for review and answers, and, if the decision may become final under paragraph (a), the date when it may become final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of Subpart H (rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart governs issuance, amendment, and repeal of regulations in which participation by interested persons is prescribed under Section 553 of title 5 U.S.C. The procedures in §§ 2.804 through 2.810 apply to all rulemakings. The procedures in §§ 2.802 through 2.803 apply to petitions for rulemaking except for certain initial design certification rulemakings; and §§ 2.811 through 2.819, as supplemented, apply to standard design certification rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which procedural provisions apply to which kinds of rulemaking and petition scenarios (general rulemaking vs. standard design certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking may be initiated by the Commission on its own instance, on recommendation of another U.S. agency, or on petition of any other interested person, including an application for design certification under specified subparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone with interest may petition; agency or other federal entities may also start rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing methods and contact information for petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may petition the Commission to issue, amend, or rescind any regulation in 10 CFR chapter I. The petition should be addressed to the Secretary, Attention: Rulemakings and Adjudications Staff, and sent by mail, email to Rulemaking.Comments@nrc.gov, or by hand delivery to the specified NRC address during business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides authorized channels for submitting petitions and contact expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on NRC staff assistance during consultation on petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In consultations regarding drafting or amendment of a petition, NRC staff may: describe the process for filing, tracking, amending, withdrawing, and resolving a petition; clarify an existing NRC regulation and its basis; and assist the petitioner to clarify a petition so the Commission can understand the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC staff will not draft or develop text or alternative approaches to address matters in the petition, nor advise whether a petition should be amended or withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content elements of a petition for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition must clearly and concisely: (i) specify the petitioner's name and contact info; (ii) if an organization, provide organizational identifying info; (iii) present specific problems/issues to be addressed including where NRC requirements are incorrect/incomplete/inadequate/unduly burdensome; (iv) cite/enclose/reference publicly-available technical, scientific, or other data supporting assertions; (v) present the petitioner's proposed solution (may include specific regulatory language); (vi) provide analysis explaining how the proposed solution solves the problems; (vii) cite/enclose/reference any other publicly-available data supporting the proposed solution; and (viii) if required by 10 CFR 51.68, submit a separate Petitioner's Environmental Report per 10 CFR 51.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be precise, provide supporting data, propose concrete regulatory language where appropriate, and include environmental documentation when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance suggestions to aid NRC evaluation of petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist NRC evaluation, the petitioner should clearly and concisely: (i) explain why the proposed rulemaking solution is within the NRC's authority to adopt; and (ii) explain why rulemaking is the most favorable approach as opposed to licensing, an order, or referral to another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explaining legal authority and the rationale for rulemaking (versus other remedies) improves the petition's chance of being docketed and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of lead petitioner for multi-signer petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is signed by multiple petitioners, the petition must designate a lead petitioner responsible for disseminating communications received from the NRC to co-petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRC communications to the lead petitioner satisfy obligations to all co-petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to suspend adjudication pending petition resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner may request the Commission to suspend all or any part of any licensing proceeding to which the petitioner is a participant pending disposition of the petition for rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must include such request with filing; presiding officer/Commission will consider suspension appropriate in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for amendment or withdrawal of docketed petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner wants to amend or withdraw a docketed petition, the petitioner should include the docket number and the date the original petition was submitted in a filing addressed to the Secretary or by email to Rulemaking.Comments@nrc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments/withdrawals should reference original docket info to ensure proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing review and sufficiency criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt NRC will acknowledge the petition and evaluate it for sufficiency according to review criteria: whether it includes required information under § 2.802(c); whether the regulatory change sought is within NRC legal authority; and whether it raises a potentially valid issue that warrants further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition lacks required info, is outside NRC authority, or does not raise a potentially valid issue, NRC will notify petitioner, explain deficiencies, and the petitioner may resubmit without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing, public posting, and Federal Register notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If docketed, a copy of the petition will be posted in ADAMS and on regulations.gov. NRC will publish a notice of docketing in the Federal Register informing the public that NRC is reviewing the merits, including the docket number and instructions on tracking the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public transparency is ensured by posting and Federal Register notice; docket number is key for tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment handling and privacy notice
rubrics_metrics.description: At its discretion, the NRC may request public comment on a docketed petition. The NRC will post all comment submissions at regulations.gov and enter them into ADAMS without removing identifying or contact information from comment submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone aggregating comments must inform contributors not to include identifying/contact information they do not want publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in NRC determination on a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Following docketing, NRC's determination on a petition may be based upon, but is not limited to: (i) the merits of the petition; (ii) the immediacy of the safety, environmental, or security concern raised; (iii) availability of NRC resources and priority relative to other rulemaking issues; (iv) whether problems are already under consideration by NRC; (v) substance of any public comment received if comment is requested; and (vi) NRC's relevant past decisions and current policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors guide whether NRC will initiate rulemaking, deny, or take other action; resource and priority considerations are explicitly part of the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure and resolution of petition docket
rubrics_metrics.description: After determining the appropriate regulatory action, NRC will administratively close the petition docket and publish a Federal Register notice describing that action, including any related Docket ID. NRC may: (i) decide not to undertake rulemaking and inform the petitioner of grounds for denial; or (ii) initiate a rulemaking action (new, ongoing, or planned) that considers the petition issues and inform the petitioner in writing of this decision and associated Docket ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution will be publicly announced in the Federal Register and reflected in ADAMS; closure may follow denial, initiation of rulemaking, or petitioner withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of petition resolution in Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: NRC will publish a Federal Register notice informing the public that it has concluded all planned regulatory action with respect to some or all of the issues presented in a petition for rulemaking. This may occur by adoption of a final rule, denial by NRC, or withdrawal by the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register notice will include discussion of how the regulatory action addresses the issue, the grounds for denial, or information on the withdrawal, as applicable.
